findings.finding: Peak movement responses in a difficult task are positively correlated with positive emotions and negatively correlated with negative emotions.
findings.quote: Peak frequency of movement responses was positively correlated with the frequency of positive emotions.

findings.finding: Increasing positive emotions and down-regulating negative emotional responses may be important for learning complex tasks.
findings.quote: increasing positive emotions, and perhaps down-regulating negative emotional responses, may be important for improving performance and learning a complex operant task in infancy.

findings.finding: Partner-assisted training leads to superior motor learning progress, motivation, attention, and positive emotions compared to robot-led training.
findings.quote: These findings suggest that partner-assisted training fosters stronger motivation, attention, and positive emotions, contributing to superior outcomes.

findings.finding: Motor coordination difficulties can place strain on wellbeing and cause a range of negative emotions when unsupported.
findings.quote: motor coordination difficulties impacted upon social and emotional wellbeing by placing strain on relationships, prompting bullying and exclusion, putting safety at risk and causing a range of negative emotions.

principle: Emotions and interpersonal interactions significantly influence motor learning and performance, where positive emotions correlate with peak performance and partner-assisted training fosters better outcomes than robotic training.
for_the_teacher: Foster positive emotions and design interactions that encourage social connection to support better motor learning outcomes.
